title: The Mended Net
logline: A fishing crew's net comes back from the water cut clean through, torn by a rival boat working too close to their ground. Before it fishes again, it has to be mended, knot by knot, on the sand.
human_question: When someone stands between us and what we need, what does the wanting turn into?

premise.story: A crew whose gear has been damaged in a dispute over fishing ground works through the practical, unglamorous business of repair: assessing the damage, arguing about what to do next, and mending the net by hand before the next tide.
premise.place: A working fishing beach where boats, gear and grounds are shared, contested and defended.
premise.experience: The viewer sits at eye level with rope and netting through a long, patient repair, while the argument about who was in the wrong keeps surfacing and subsiding.

concept_links.why: Pradeepika's own example shows a wish turning to hatred the moment something living stands in its way [C007-P:L59]. A rival boat working another crew's ground is exactly that turn: the catch is wanted, the other boat is the obstacle, and the mind's response to a threatened livelihood is named in the sources as a common occasion for this state [C007-P:L49].

Fishing ground is one of the five things stinginess clings to (āvāsa, one's 'dwelling' or territory) [C022-P:L133; C022-M:L43]. The dispute over grounds is a territorial version of that same clinging, seen from the outside rather than named as a fault in anyone.

what_camera_could_observe: The net brought in and laid out, the cut examined by hand
The crew's first words on seeing the damage
Mending: shuttle, twine, the repeated motion of tying knots
Conversation about the other boat and the shared ground, however it actually goes
The mended net going back out, or staying ashore if it is not ready
what_must_be_real: The damage, the dispute and the repair must be real and already in progress or freshly happened; nothing is cut, staged or provoked for the camera. Any account of the other crew must be presented as one side's view, not as settled fact.

possible_arc.opening: A torn net laid out on sand, the tear still fresh.
possible_arc.turn: The talk of blame gives way to the slow, wordless work of mending.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever the crew decides to do about the other boat, and whether the net is ready in time, ends the film as it actually happens.

position_hint: opening candidate: a mended net is a plain, real form of Object 3's mark of conflict, damage and repair, and a torn or mended piece of gear could be a natural moment for its acquisition if a crew genuinely offers or discards one

requirements: A fishing community with a real, current or recent dispute over grounds or gear
A crew willing to show the damage and the repair, and to speak about the dispute on their own terms
Access that does not require naming or filming the other side without consent

suggestions.name: Fishing villages of the Jaffna peninsula coast
suggestions.why: A coastline with many small fishing communities and long-contested inshore grounds; well known as an active fishing region.
suggestions.verify: Confirm a specific community, a real current dispute, and willingness to be filmed discussing it.

suggestions.name: Fishing beaches of the eastern coast
suggestions.region: Trincomalee or Batticaloa district, Eastern Province
suggestions.why: Another well-known active fishing coastline where inshore ground disputes are a known feature of the livelihood.
suggestions.verify: Confirm a specific community and a real, current dispute.

risks: Taking one crew's side in a real, ongoing dispute
Filming or naming the rival crew without their consent
Turning a livelihood dispute into a simple morality tale
drop_if: No crew will discuss the dispute openly, or filming would inflame a live conflict
The damage was not caused by a genuine dispute and would need to be invented

connections.note: Both are opening candidates where Object 3's mark of repair could plausibly be acquired; only one should open the group.
Two fishing-community films: one scarred by a dispute over what is claimed, the other testing what is freely shared at the catch.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
